instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, drain the tofu and cut it into 1 inch cubes. Pat the cubes very dry with paper towels.
Cut each tomato into 6 wedges. Mince the garlic. Slice the green onions, keeping the white and green parts apart.

Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the tofu in a single layer and leave it alone for 4 minutes, until the underside is golden. Turn the cubes and cook for 4 minutes, until golden on most sides.
Transfer the tofu to a plate. Leave the oil in the skillet and turn the heat to medium.
Add the white parts of the green onions and stir for 30 seconds. Add 1 tbsp tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens. Add the garlic and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they soften and start to break down.
Add 1/2 cup water, 1 tbsp tamari, 2 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 8 minutes, until the sauce is thick.
Add the tofu and stir gently to coat it. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the tofu and sauce over the rice and sprinkle with the green parts of the green onions.
method_notes: Every version fries the tofu first, then simmers it in a sauce of fresh tomatoes with tomato paste, sugar and salt, and serves it over rice with green onions. The lead deep-fries and presses the tofu for 30 minutes; this pan-browns it after patting it dry, as the Runaway Rice and vegan versions do. The lead's optional fish sauce is replaced with tamari so it stays vegan and gluten-free, and garlic and the green onion whites come from the other versions. No source had 20 or more ratings; the lead is the best-rated readable one.
